description: Fold BMI into the pure recommendation engine as a deterministic post-process layer, preserving ALL existing safety invariants (R1 heavy guard always wins, canOfferAggressive stays the sole aggressive gatekeeper, BMI never widens aggressive eligibility). Add the caring underweight note and firmer overweight/obese framing to copy.ts, and extend the recommendation tests with BMI cases. Depends on FEAT-001 (requires heightCm/weightKg on ProfilingAnswers and src/lib/bmi.ts).
steps: In src/lib/recommendation.ts, import { computeBmi, bmiCategory } and the BmiCategory type from @/lib/bmi. Add a pure function `applyBmiAdjustment(base: Recommendation, category: BmiCategory, answers: ProfilingAnswers): Recommendation` with a block comment stating the chosen approach: BMI is a post-process that sharpens but never overrides safety; the R1 heavy branch returns BEFORE this runs so a heavy exerciser is never BMI-adjusted; canOfferAggressive remains the sole gatekeeper and BMI never adds 20:4/omad.

Implement applyBmiAdjustment rules: underweight -> if base.method is stricter than 14:10 (i.e. anything other than 14:10) set method to 14:10; filter alternatives to drop 18:6/20:4/omad (keep 16:8 only); set warning to a non-null caring underweight note (reuse base.warning concatenation only if needed, but underweight warning must always be present) and prepend/append the caring note to rationale; this must surface even when the goal would otherwise suggest a stricter method. normal -> return base unchanged. overweight/obese -> only when answers.goal === 'weight_loss' AND canOfferAggressive(answers) is already true, reorder alternatives so 18:6 appears earlier (more prominent) WITHOUT adding any new aggressive method, and append a firmer-but-safe note to rationale; keep base.method as the gentle default (never auto-jump to 20:4/omad). For all other goals/states, return base unchanged.

In recommendMethod, keep the R1 heavy early return exactly as-is (return buildHeavy() before any BMI logic). After the switch(goal) produces `base`, compute `const category = bmiCategory(computeBmi(answers.heightCm, answers.weightKg))` and return `applyBmiAdjustment(base, category, answers)`. Do not change the exerciseState or canOfferAggressive logic.

In src/lib/copy.ts under the existing `recommendation` block add new non-empty, Indonesian, emoji-free strings: an underweight caring note (advise against aggressive fasting, prioritize adequate nutritious intake) and an overweight/obese firmer-but-safe note. Reference them from applyBmiAdjustment. Do not remove or renumber existing R1-R16 strings.

Update src/lib/__tests__/recommendation.test.ts: confirm the FEAT-001 helper change (normal-BMI defaults) keeps all R1-R16 rows and the 25-input invariant block green. ADD a new describe block for BMI with cases: (a) underweight + a goal that would otherwise suggest 18:6 (e.g. metabolic/none) yields a method that is NOT 18:6/20:4/omad (expect 14:10 or 16:8 per the rule) and a non-null warning containing the caring note; (b) heavy exerciser with underweight AND with obese BMI still yields 14:10 + non-null warning (BMI never overrides the heavy guard); (c) canOfferAggressive stays false for every non-weight-loss goal and for moderate/heavy regardless of BMI (assert directly over obese/underweight inputs); (d) overweight and obese + weight_loss + none/light never produce 20:4/omad as the primary method, and 18:6 is present in alternatives. All asserted rationale/warning strings are non-empty.
acceptance_criteria: recommendMethod remains pure and deterministic; the R1 heavy guard still returns 14:10 + non-null warning for any goal and any BMI.
applyBmiAdjustment exists with a comment documenting the post-process approach and never adds 20:4/omad; canOfferAggressive is unchanged and remains the sole aggressive gatekeeper.
Underweight inputs are never recommended 18:6/20:4/omad as the primary method and always carry the caring note in warning/rationale.
overweight/obese + weight_loss never auto-jumps the primary to 20:4/omad.
New recommendation BMI test cases pass and all pre-existing recommendation assertions still pass.
No-emoji scan passes for the new copy strings.
findings:
DONE. tsc --noEmit clean; full suite 184 passed (was 174 after FEAT-001; +10 new recommendation cases); recommendation.test.ts 61, no-emoji scan green.

src/lib/recommendation.ts: imported { bmiCategory, computeBmi, type BmiCategory } from @/lib/bmi. Added exported pure fn `applyBmiAdjustment(base: Recommendation, category: BmiCategory, answers: ProfilingAnswers): Recommendation` with a block comment documenting the post-process approach (sharpens/softens but never overrides safety; R1 heavy returns before it; canOfferAggressive stays sole gatekeeper; never adds 20:4/omad; normal incl. NaN returns base unchanged). recommendMethod now builds `base` from the switch(goal) (refactored each case to assign+break; exhaustiveness `never` default preserved) then returns applyBmiAdjustment(base, bmiCategory(computeBmi(heightCm, weightKg)), answers). R1 heavy early-return is unchanged and still runs BEFORE BMI. exerciseState/canOfferAggressive logic untouched.

ADJUSTMENT RULES: underweight -> primary softened to 14:10 if base.method is anything stricter (NON_GENTLE = 16:8/18:6/20:4/omad), alternatives filtered to drop 18:6/20:4/omad (16:8 may remain), warning ALWAYS set to copy.recommendation.underweightNote, rationale prefixed with copy.recommendation.underweightRationale. normal -> returns base by reference. overweight|obese -> ONLY when goal==='weight_loss' AND canOfferAggressive(answers) already true: reorder alternatives to pull an ALREADY-PRESENT 18:6 to front (never adds it), append copy.recommendation.overweightNote to rationale, primary stays gentle (never 20:4/omad); otherwise returns base unchanged.

src/lib/copy.ts: added under the recommendation block (no R1-R16 strings removed/renumbered): `underweightNote`, `underweightRationale`, `overweightNote` — all non-empty Indonesian Gojek voice, emoji-free.

FEAT-003 NOTE: the underweight caring note is delivered via the `warning` field (string | null). RecommendationStep already renders rec.warning in its warning banner (per context.json), so the underweight note surfaces with NO markup change in RecommendationStep. Overweight/obese framing is appended to rationale (no separate field). applyBmiAdjustment is exported if FEAT-003 UI needs to preview category effects, but recommendMethod already applies it internally. BMI inputs flow through answers.heightCm/weightKg (mandatory per FEAT-001); invalid/NaN BMI -> bmiCategory returns 'normal' -> no adjustment, so a partially-filled BmiStep never destabilizes the recommendation.

Typescript gotcha for FEAT-003: when reordering MethodId[] with a spread + a string literal, annotate the array as `MethodId[]` or the literal widens to string (hit this; fixed by annotating `const alternatives: MethodId[]`).
